clue.text: Old port with a square meal

definitions.meaning: ... in Kent was one of the medieval Cinque Ports, now silted up and inland
bread with a filling, often cut into squares, eaten as a meal

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives at an ancient harbour town and sits down to a hearty dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDWICH is a town in Kent, once one of the Cinque Ports, the old group of English Channel harbours; 'with' just joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town and the filled bread snack share one name, the snack being named after an Earl of that town.

clue.text: Nothing new about this establishment, presumably

definitions.text: Nothing new about this establishment, presumably

parts.words: Nothing new about this establishment, presumably
parts.note: a shop where none of the stock is new, because every item has had a previous owner

explanation.surface: A grumble that a business has no fresh ideas at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'nothing new' as a complaint about stale ideas; in fact it describes a shop selling only used goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop dealing in used goods by definition stocks nothing new.

clue.text: Always heroic? Certainly not

definitions.meaning: someone always heroic would be without fright, read as a phrase
the British colloquial exclamation of refusal, 'not likely!'

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are brave every single time firmly says no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No fear!' is everyday British slang for 'Not a chance!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking fright describes a hero, and the same phrase is a British exclamation meaning not on your life.

clue.text: Pain at parting from right girl

indicators.note: the letter for right splits the word for girl into two parts, so it sits inside it

parts.note: wench is an old word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone feels the hurt of saying goodbye to the girl who suits them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' puts R inside WENCH; 'at' and 'from' are link words. The surface pulls 'Pain at parting' together as one phrase, which is also a fair gloss of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden sharp pang, especially the emotional hurt of a painful separation.

clue.text: May I not purchase a large supporting bracket?

parts.note: read as 'can't I', a question asking whether one is not able
purchase means leverage or grip, and a lever gives purchase

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether they may not buy a big wall bracket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like buying but means mechanical grip. 'May I not' turns into the contraction CAN'T I.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a long projecting beam or bracket fixed at one end that holds up a balcony or bridge span.

clue.text: No-this isn't a suitable call

parts.note: in the card game bridge, putting this word after 'No' makes a bid meaning the hand is played with no suit as master suit

explanation.surface: A complaint that a particular telephone call was inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the bid 'No trumps' means no suit outranks the others; the clue puns on 'suit' since the call names no suit. 'call' is a bid, not a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards of the master suit in a card game carry the name, and in bridge the bid without one is 'No' plus that word.

clue.text: Famished as a bird we follow round

indicators.note: the word for we comes after the round letter, following it in the answer

parts.note: the raven is a large black bird of the crow family
O is round in shape
us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: We trail behind a hungry crow-like bird circling overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' places US after O; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means extremely hungry, a synonym of starving.

clue.text: Tree from island wood

parts.note: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea
a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: A tree is taken from a wood on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The mangrove is a tropical shrub or small tree growing in coastal swamps.

clue.text: Vessels that can be boiling hot

definitions.meaning: things giving off vapour, or cooking pots that cook food over boiling water

explanation.surface: A warning that some containers can get scalding hot.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is ships driven by steam, the other things that steam when very hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam-driven ships and pans that cook food in vapour share the name, both linked to boiling water.

clue.text: It appears to put iron in French coffee

indicators.note: to put something into the coffee is to place it inside, so the following pieces go within the word for French coffee

parts.note: café is the French word for coffee
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written: the little word itself joins the iron

explanation.surface: A remark that iron seems to have been added to a French coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the definition, the stimulant found in coffee; 'appears to' is link. The little word 'in' is fodder here, not the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The stimulant alkaloid found in coffee and tea is what the clue's 'It' refers to, coffee being its best-known source.

clue.text: Line of approach to a meeting-place

parts.note: a venue is the place where an event or meeting happens

explanation.surface: Directions on how to reach the place where a gathering is held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; the definition looks like part of the directions.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a tree-lined road leading to a house, or figuratively a way of approach.

clue.text: Tyneside suffering the rigours of a polar region?

definitions.text: Tyneside suffering the rigours of a polar region?

parts.words: Tyneside suffering the rigours of a polar region?
parts.note: Tyneside lies in the north-east (NE) of England, and frozen conditions there would be polar ones

explanation.surface: Newcastle shivering in Arctic-style weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England, abbreviated NE; add the polar word to get a biogeographical region covering North America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nearctic is the biogeographic realm of North America, reaching up into the frozen far north.

clue.text: Place to put a worker on edge

indicators.note: the worker sits on, so before, the edge in this across answer

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword worker
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Advice on where to station an employee who is nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county in Northern Ireland. 'on edge' looks like nerves but is placement; 'to put' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Northern Irish county and town, so it is a geographical location.

clue.text: The one mistake which proved decisive?

definitions.text: The one mistake which proved decisive?

parts.words: The one mistake which proved decisive?
parts.note: a mistake that decides the outcome is a crucial or fatal one

explanation.surface: Looking back on the single slip that settled a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip described as essential or critical is one that determines the result.

clue.text: Staff note produced in half a shake

parts.note: semi- is a prefix meaning half
a quaver is a trill or shake in the voice

explanation.surface: An employee's memo knocked out in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is the musical stave, not employees; 'in half a shake' looks like 'very quickly'. 'produced in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixteenth note written on the stave lasts half the time of a quaver, so it is a musical note.

clue.text: See 1 down
Nothing more than a notion, say, about …

definitions.text: Nothing more than a notion, say, about …

parts.words: Nothing more than a notion, say, about …
parts.note: nothing more than gives the adjective 'only', and a notion is a thought, leading on into the next clue

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a plan as only a thought, then trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one, but this answer is simply 'only a thought'.
explanation.definitionFit: An only-just-formed thought with no substance is a passing fancy.

clue.text: … a weird-sounding North American waterway

parts.note: a Great Lake whose name is pronounced like a word for weird or spooky

explanation.surface: Continuing a story about some strange river in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The second word sounds like 'eerie', meaning weird; the lake lies between the USA and Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes on the US-Canadian border, so a North American body of water.

clue.text: Standard description for any Tom, Dick or Harry?

definitions.text: Standard description for any Tom, Dick or Harry?

parts.words: Standard description for any Tom, Dick or Harry?
parts.note: Tom, Dick or Harry stands for any ordinary person, and a standard or typical person fits the phrase

explanation.surface: Asking how to label any ordinary chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Any Tom, Dick or Harry' is an idiom for anybody at all; 'Standard' means typical, not a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The typical ordinary person is the mean, middling figure, the usual idiom for a nobody in particular.

clue.text: A close source of relief in affliction

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are the raw source from which the answer is reworked

explanation.surface: A nearby provider of help to those in distress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' signals that the letters of A CLOSE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort or consolation given in times of distress.

clue.text: One who sees the pitcher after six

indicators.note: the jug comes after the numeral in the answer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
an ewer is a large jug or pitcher

explanation.surface: A spectator watches the bowler after the sixth ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitcher' suggests baseball or cricket bowling but here means a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer is a person who watches or looks at something, an onlooker.

clue.text: Tom taking forty winks?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, and forty winks is a short sleep, so this is a feline having a doze

explanation.surface: A man named Tom having a quick snooze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A short daytime doze, named after the way cats sleep briefly.

clue.text: Type of engine one finds in Leeds broken down

indicators.note: the letters are broken apart and put back together in a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An engine found to have failed in a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken down' rearranges I and LEEDS; 'finds in' is link. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A compression-ignition engine using heavy oil fuel, named after its German inventor.

clue.text: Flower-for one cent in an Italian city

indicators.note: the pieces for one and cent are placed inside the city

parts.note: Verona is a city in northern Italy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bloom sold for a single cent in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places IC inside VERONA; 'for' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, or speedwell, is a small blue-flowered plant.

clue.text: Ivy's other name being dear in a way

parts.note: a he is a male being, as in 'is it a he or a she?'

indicators.note: the word dear is rearranged, laid out in a different way

explanation.surface: A woman called Ivy has a pet name that is affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' rearranges DEAR to DERA. 'Ivy' looks like a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the Latin botanical genus name for the climbing evergreen plant.

clue.text: Watering turned out to be a huge success

indicators.note: the letters are turned out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener's watering paid off splendidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'proved to be' but signals an anagram of WATERING.
explanation.definitionFit: A big victory is a triumph, a huge success.

clue.text: Nattered on for being charged-a penny-levy

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
rated means assessed for rates, the local levy on property

explanation.surface: Someone talked at length about being charged a penny tax.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British local property tax, so to be rated is to be assessed for that levy; 'for being charged' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to talk foolishly at length, so prated means chattered on.

clue.text: Priceless journey?

parts.note: priceless read as 'without a price', so a journey costing nothing

explanation.surface: An outing so wonderful its value cannot be measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless' normally means invaluable; here it means having no price.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing provided at no charge to the traveller, costing nothing.
